Ask only context that changes tempo authority, then present one reversible experiment: Preserve the current project, set the affected duplicate region to ignore tempo, compare it to the original file at native speed, then reanalyze only if conformance is desired. Restore the previous map or region state, then change only the most likely wrong assumption and replay the identical section.
The BPM or tempo-map change barely affected what I hear.
Explain what the null result rules out, verify downbeat/meter/source authority, and choose one smaller diagnostic check.
Why did that happen, and what should I learn from it?

Explain the causal principle in plain language and connect it to the exact A/B: An imported recording usually changes speed because it was told to follow project tempo using incorrect or unintended tempo data. First restore native playback, then diagnose metadata, analysis, and region follow state.
